note: Adapted from the identification and measurements of Pinzón-Florián (2022), in English; that work is a new record for Colombia, the morphological description being quoted from the original description of Engel & Krishna (2007), together with measurements and figure notes for the Colombian specimens. This entry therefore has only a soldier and a nymph section, and the measurements are limited to the specimens collected.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The largest species in the genus, especially the soldier (Engel & Krishna 2007). Colombian specimens: major soldier head length including the mandibles 2.62 mm, head width 1.68 mm, pronotum width 0.89 mm, agreeing with the measurements given in the original description; those of the minor soldier (head length including the labrum, labrum length, head width, pronotum length and width) slightly larger than recorded by Engel & Krishna (2007). Labrum: in the major soldier the labrum is elongate, slightly widened at the tip, the apical margin rounded and without a notch, with a shallow longitudinal dorsal depression running back from the apical margin for about half the labrum length; in the minor soldier the labrum is distinctly forked at the tip, with several erect pale yellow setae at the tip and scattered short pale yellow setae over the rest of the dorsal surface, slightly more numerous in the apical half. The head of the minor soldier is "gently convex, the sides convergent anteriorly, slightly convergent posteriorly from the midpoint to the gently rounded posterior margin", which differs slightly from the Colombian specimens of this species, in which the anterior margin of the pronotum is wide and trilobed (recorded as rounded in the original description). Mandibular dentition (Engel & Krishna 2007): the left mandible has two thick teeth, one slightly before and one slightly after the midpoint, the anterior tooth distinctly longer than the posterior, the posterior margin of the anterior tooth slightly curved and the posterior tooth straight; the right mandible has two teeth near the middle, the anterior shorter than the posterior, both shorter than those of the left mandible, the posterior tooth running straight in from the inner mandibular surface and the anterior tooth closer to the mandibular surface.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: The alate nymph is distinctly larger than the other castes: body, legs, head and antennae yellow with a light brown tinge. Head capsule oval, almost as wide as the pronotum, densely covered with long setae. Moniliform antennae 20-segmented, covered with long setae, the basal flagellomere distinctly larger than segment 2. Eyes dark brown with pale margins; two ocelli, pale, not projecting, far from the compound eyes. Clypeus elongate-oval, the margins rounded, covered with long setae. Pronotum with rounded margins, wider anteriorly, with scattered long setae, the anterior margin with several shorter erect setae; the posterior margin slightly concave in the middle. Single alate nymph: head width 2.1 mm, head length to the apex of the labrum 2.1 mm, pronotum width 2.5 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Distribution: Ecuador (type locality), Peru, Bolivia, and Colombia (Pensilvania, Caldas Department, altitude 2100 m) as a new record, taken in decaying wood in secondary forest. Other known species of the genus: D. japuraensis (Amazonian Brazil), D. latilabrum (Bolivia), D. longidens (Panama), D. longilabius (Brazil, French Guiana, Guyana, Trinidad), D. neli (French Guiana), D. tenebrosus (Guyana).
